title: Carrying Capacity and Population Growth Practice Exam
description: Recall and guided drill for Carrying Capacity and Population Growth.

questions.question: What is carrying capacity?
options: the largest population an ecosystem can support over time
the number of animals born in one day
the speed of an individual organism
the total number of species on Earth
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity describes supportable population size.

questions.question: Food, water, space, disease, and predation are examples of ________ factors.
Carrying capacity can change if habitat quality or resource supply changes.
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity depends on environmental conditions.

questions.question: What happens as a population approaches carrying capacity?
Explain why an S-shaped growth curve levels off.
questions.correctAnswer: It levels off because limiting factors such as food, space, disease, and competition reduce growth as the population nears carrying capacity.
questions.explanation: The answer should connect resource limits to slower growth.

questions.question: Which situation is an overshoot?
options: a population rises above what resources can support and later declines
a population remains exactly stable forever
an ecosystem has no limiting factors
questions.explanation: Overshoot occurs when population exceeds supportable size.

questions.question: A population can grow rapidly forever if it starts small.
questions.explanation: Growth is eventually limited by resources and other factors.

questions.question: Give one example of a limiting factor and explain its effect.
questions.correctAnswer: Food shortage can reduce survival and reproduction, slowing population growth.
questions.explanation: Any valid limiting factor with effect is acceptable.
